"See You Again" was written by [[DJ Frank E]], [[Charlie Puth]], [[Wiz Khalifa]], Andrew Cedar, [[Dann Hume]], Phoebe Cockburn, and Joshua Karl Simon Hardy.<ref name="Credits"/> It was produced by DJ Frank E, Charlie Puth, Andrew Cedar, [[Kevin Weaver]], and [[Mike Caren]] with mixing provided by [[Manny Marroquin]].<ref name="Credits"/> Frank E and Puth were approached by their publishing company, Artist Publishing Group, to develop a melody that could pay tribute to actor [[Paul Walker]] for the film ''[[Furious 7]]'' (2015); Artist Publishing Group then set up a first-time studio session for Puth with DJ Frank E at a studio in Los Angeles.<ref name="Samantha Highfill">{{cite magazine|author=Highfill, Samantha|url=http://www.ew.com/article/2015/04/07/charlie-puth-see-you-again-paul-walker|title=Charlie Puth talks writing 'See You Again' for Paul Walker's goodbye|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=April 7, 2015|access-date=April 11, 2015}}</ref>

Puth, talking about the first studio session for the song, said that when he went to the studio "[the producers] were working on this song" and it already had the "See You Again" chords, but it was a "[[Synthesizer|synthy]]" production for a "[[Electronic dance music|dance]] song", and he later suggested the idea of the song being a [[piano ballad]] instead.<ref name="HS"/> Puth said that he became emotionally attached while writing the lyrics of the track, recalling Vail Cerullo, a friend of Puth's from his time at [[Berklee College of Music]], who died in a motorcycle accident in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehill.org/RelId/1175740/ISvars/default/Vail_Cerullo_09_Remembered_in_Number_1_Billboard_Hit_Fast_and_Furious_Theme_Song.htm|title=The Hill School -> Vail Cerullo '09 Remembered in Number 1 Billboard Hit & Fast and Furious Theme Song|website=www.thehill.org|access-date=March 23, 2017|archive-date=March 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170324084224/http://www.thehill.org/RelId/1175740/ISvars/default/Vail_Cerullo_09_Remembered_in_Number_1_Billboard_Hit_Fast_and_Furious_Theme_Song.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/local/See-You-Again-Charlie-Puth-Wiz-Khalifa-Vail-Cerullo-Furious-7-303504911.html|title=Local Man Inspires Hit "Furious 7" Song|publisher=[[WCAU]]|date=May 12, 2015}}</ref> Puth and DJ Frank E's output from the session was well received by ''Furious 7'' filmmakers, [[Universal Pictures]], and Atlantic. As a result, the track was further commissioned to include rapped verses based on the subject of family, combined with Puth's vocals and a piano [[melody]]. The song then went through an extensive note-giving and production process.<ref name="LA"/> Before choosing Wiz Khalifa's version, several other rappers were offered to record the rapped parts of the song, including [[Eminem]], [[50 Cent]] and [[Tyga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fuse.tv/2016/01/50-cent-eminem-turned-down-see-you-again-wiz-khalifa|title=50 Cent: Eminem Turned Down Wiz Khalifa's "See You Again"|publisher=Fuse TV|access-date=December 26, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.36980/title.50-cent-eminem-turned-down-see-you-again-record|title=50 Cent & Eminem Turned Down "See You Again" Record|magazine=[[HipHopDX]]|date=January 11, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mtv.com/news/55n62m/chris-brown-tyga-wiz-khalifa-see-you-again-remix|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231226193952/https://www.mtv.com/news/55n62m/chris-brown-tyga-wiz-khalifa-see-you-again-remix|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 26, 2023|title=Chris Brown And Tyga Join Wiz Khalifa In This 'See You Again' Remix: Listen|publisher=MTV News|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=December 26, 2023}}</ref> Puth said that he was initially reluctant to let the film's soundtrack label, [[Atlantic Records]], choose his vocals for the song. "See You Again" was written by DJ Frank E, Charlie Puth, Wiz Khalifa, Andrew Cedar, Dann Hume, Phoebe Cockburn, and Joshua Karl Simon Hardy. It was produced by DJ Frank E, Charlie Puth, Andrew Cedar, Kevin Weaver, and Mike Caren with mixing provided by Manny Marroquin. Frank E and Puth were approached by their publishing company, Artist Publishing Group, to develop a melody that could pay tribute to actor Paul Walker for the film Furious 7 (2015); Artist Publishing Group then set up a first-time studio session for Puth with DJ Frank E at a studio in Los Angeles.

Puth, talking about the first studio session for the song, said that when he went to the studio "[the producers] were working on this song" and it already had the "See You Again" chords, but it was a "synthy" production for a "dance song", and he later suggested the idea of the song being a piano ballad instead. Puth said that he became emotionally attached while writing the lyrics of the track, recalling Vail Cerullo, a friend of Puth's from his time at Berklee College of Music, who died in a motorcycle accident in 2012. Puth and DJ Frank E's output from the session was well received by Furious 7 filmmakers, Universal Pictures, and Atlantic. As a result, the track was further commissioned to include rapped verses based on the subject of family, combined with Puth's vocals and a piano melody. The song then went through an extensive note-giving and production process. Before choosing Wiz Khalifa's version, several other rappers were offered to record the rapped parts of the song, including Eminem, 50 Cent and Tyga. Puth said that he was initially reluctant to let the film's soundtrack label, Atlantic Records, choose his vocals for the song. In an interview with the Los Angeles Times, Puth recalled, "It just seemed to occur from out of nowhere. And basically 10 minutes later Justin (DJ Frank E) and I wrote it, we sent it off, and I thought we'd never hear about it again". Puth revealed on The Howard Stern Show that Atlantic originally wanted to get a more established singer to sing his part, having Chris Brown, Sam Smith, Jason Derulo and others recording their own versions of the song's chorus. Puth stated that also British singer Adele "wanted to cut it". According to Puth, "none of the vocals had the [right] feeling ... What I was singing about specifically, you just couldn't hear it in their voice. I think Chris Brown got the closest to it, but they ended up, lucky me, going with my vocal".

The song was chosen to be played at the end of the film. After Brian O'Conner's retirement send-off, the song can be heard as Brian and Dominic Toretto drive on a mountain road, parting ways as they reach a fork.

In the United States, "See You Again" debuted on the Billboard Hot 100 and Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs charts dated March 19, 2015, at number 100 and number 29 respectively, with first-week sales of 25,000 copies. On the chart issued for April 18, 2015, the song climbed from number 84 to number ten on the Billboard Hot 100, selling 168,000 copies as the chart's "Digital Gainer" that week. Its climb into the top ten was the chart's biggest since Katy Perry's "Roar" (2013). In its fifth week, "See You Again" sold 464,000 copies and rose from number ten to number one on the Billboard Hot 100. The song marked Khalifa's second number one on the chart, following "Black and Yellow" (2011), and Puth's first. It topped the Billboard Hot 100 chart for 12 non-consecutive weeks. After its 12th week it was finally knocked off the top spot by Omi{{'}}s hit, "Cheerleader". It is one of 33 songs to reach number one for at least 10 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100. The song also topped the Mainstream Top 40 and Rhythmic charts for four weeks and three weeks respectively. The song also topped Hot Rap Songs and Hot R&B Hip Hip Songs for 14 weeks each. As of July 7, 2016, "See You Again" has sold a total of 4,122,938 copies in the United States. The song would later be certified 14xPlatinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for equivalent sales of 14 million units in the United States.

The song holds the record for the most-streamed track in a single day on Spotify in the United States. It set the record for most streams in a single week worldwide during April 6 to April 12 (streamed 21.9 million times), and in the United Kingdom in a single week (streamed 3.72 million times from April 20 to April 26, 2015), which was broken by Justin Bieber{{'}}s "What Do You Mean?" (streamed 3.87 million times from September 17 to September 23, 2015).

The song also broke the streaming record in the United Kingdom that week with a total of 3.68 million streams that week. It marked Khalifa's second number one on the chart—following his feature on Maroon 5's "Payphone" (2012)—and Puth's first. "See You Again" sold 142,000 units during its first week at number one, and broke its own streaming record with 3.72 million streams that week. The song's climb to number one was the largest in Australian Singles Chart history.

Charlie Puth [Official Video] Furious 7 Soundtrack|date=April 6, 2015|publisher=[[YouTube]]|access-date=October 1, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/249396/top-youtube-videos-views/|title=Most Viewed Videos|work=statista.com|access-date=October 1, 2026}}</ref> It was the second video ever to record two billion<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=http://ew.com/article/2016/09/07/wiz-khalifa-charlie-puth-see-you-again-2-billion-views-youtube/|title=Wiz Khalifa and Charlie Puth's 'See You Again' Video Hits 2 Billion YouTube Views|last=Lawrence|first=Derek|date=September 7, 2016|magazine=Entertainment Weekly|access-date=May 22, 2017}}</ref> and three billion views,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2017/08/06/wiz-khalifa-charlie-puths-see-you-again-has-now-hit-three-billion-views-on-youtube/|title=Wiz Khalifa & Charlie Puth's 'See You Again' Has Now Hit Three Billion Views On YouTube|date=August 6, 2017|access-date=October 26, 2020|work=[[Forbes]]}}</ref> the third video ever to reach four billion views<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2019/03/07/wiz-khalifa-and-charlie-puths-see-you-again-is-the-third-video-to-reach-this-milestone-on-youtube/|title=Wiz Khalifa And Charlie Puth's 'See You Again' Is The Third Video To Reach This Milestone On YouTube|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=October 26, 2020|work=[[Forbes]]}}</ref> and the fourth video ever to reach five billion views.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2021/03/08/there-are-now-four-music-videos-on-youtube-that-have-accrued-five-billion-views/|title=There Are Now Four Music Videos On YouTube That Have Accrued Five Billion Views|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=March 11, 2021|work=[[Forbes]]}}</ref>
sections.text: The "See You Again" music video was the most-viewed video on YouTube from July 10 to August 4, 2017, and the most-liked video on the site from August 27, 2016, to July 25, 2017. As of October 1, 2026, it has received over 7.1 billion views and over 47 million likes, making it the site's eight most-viewed and third most-liked video. It was the second video ever to record two billion and three billion views, the third video ever to reach four billion views and the fourth video ever to reach five billion views.

sections.heading: Synopsis
sections.wikitext: The video begins with a shot of a cliff top at sunset, followed by Khalifa walking down a highway road. Puth is then shown singing the chorus whilst sitting at, and playing, a piano located between two cars. Khalifa's rap verses and Puth singing the second chorus and [[Bridge (music)|bridge]] are interspersed with footage from ''Furious 7''. After the bridge, the final movie scene shows [[Dominic Toretto]] ([[Vin Diesel]]) and [[Brian O'Conner]] ([[Cody Walker (actor)|Cody Walker]], filling in for his brother, Paul) driving together, pulled over in their cars and smiling at each other one last time before driving away on separate roads into the sunset. After the camera pans up into the sky, the screen turns white, the words "For Paul" appear on screen and the video ends.
sections.text: The video begins with a shot of a cliff top at sunset, followed by Khalifa walking down a highway road. Puth is then shown singing the chorus whilst sitting at, and playing, a piano located between two cars. Khalifa's rap verses and Puth singing the second chorus and bridge are interspersed with footage from Furious 7. After the bridge, the final movie scene shows Dominic Toretto (Vin Diesel) and Brian O'Conner (Cody Walker, filling in for his brother, Paul) driving together, pulled over in their cars and smiling at each other one last time before driving away on separate roads into the sunset. After the camera pans up into the sky, the screen turns white, the words "For Paul" appear on screen and the video ends.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext: The video was the [[list of most-viewed YouTube videos#Historical most-viewed videos|most viewed video on YouTube]] from July 10, 2017, when it surpassed "[[Gangnam Style (music video)|Gangnam Style]]" by [[Psy]],<ref name="ABC Media"/> to August 4 of that year, when it was surpassed by "[[Despacito]]" by [[Luis Fonsi]] featuring [[Daddy Yankee]].<ref name="Forbes Media"/> At 25 days, this is the shortest reign for this title since 2008. The video was nominated for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Hip-Hop Video|Best Hip-Hop Video]] and [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Collaboration|Best Collaboration]] at the [[2015 MTV Video Music Awards]], but lost both.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/events/vma/6634773/2015-mtv-vma-nominees|last=Stutz|first=Colin|title=2015 MTV Video Music Awards Nominees Revealed: Taylor Swift, Kendrick Lamar, Ed Sheeran & More|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=July 21, 2015|access-date=July 21, 2015}}</ref> On August 27, 2016, the music video surpassed "Gangnam Style" as YouTube's [[List of most-liked YouTube videos|most liked video of all time]], after "Gangnam Style" held the record for almost 4 years.<ref name="Guinness"/>
sections.text: The video was the most viewed video on YouTube from July 10, 2017, when it surpassed "Gangnam Style" by Psy, to August 4 of that year, when it was surpassed by "Despacito" by Luis Fonsi featuring Daddy Yankee. At 25 days, this is the shortest reign for this title since 2008. The video was nominated for Best Hip-Hop Video and Best Collaboration at the 2015 MTV Video Music Awards, but lost both. On August 27, 2016, the music video surpassed "Gangnam Style" as YouTube's most liked video of all time, after "Gangnam Style" held the record for almost 4 years.

sections.heading: Live performances
sections.wikitext:
Khalifa and Puth performed "See You Again" live on ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon]]'' in March 2015 and on an episode of ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' in May 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.musictimes.com/articles/32081/20150317/wiz-khalifa-furious-7-see-you-again-tonight-show-taylor-swift.htm|title=Wiz Khalifa Performs 'Furious 7' Song 'See You Again' on 'The Tonight Show,' Fumbles Taylor Swift Catchphrase Question|author=Christ, Shawn|work=Music Times|date=March 17, 2015|access-date=April 5, 2015}}</ref> Diesel also performed the song live as a tribute to Paul Walker during the [[2015 MTV Movie Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/2131149/vin-diesel-paul-walker-tribute/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150419030056/http://www.mtv.com/news/2131149/vin-diesel-paul-walker-tribute/|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 19, 2015|title=Vin Diesel Sings 'See You Again' For Paul Walker And We Have So Many Emotions|last=Bell|first=Amanda|publisher=[[MTV News]]|date=April 12, 2015|access-date=April 18, 2015}}</ref> Khalifa and Puth reprised the song in a performance on ''[[The Ellen DeGeneres Show]]'' in April 2015.<ref>{{cite web|author=Fleischer, Adam|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/2135640/wiz-khalifa-see-you-again-performance-on-ellen/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150419052722/http://www.mtv.com/news/2135640/wiz-khalifa-see-you-again-performance-on-ellen/|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 19, 2015|title=Wiz Khalifa's 'See You Again' Performance On 'Ellen' Is As Touching As The Video|date=April 16, 2015|publisher=MTV News|access-date=April 25, 2015}}</ref> Khalifa and Puth also performed the song at the [[2016 Kids' Choice Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/music-news/kids-choice-awards-2016-wiz-873961/|title=Kids' Choice Awards: Wiz Khalifa Joins Charlie Puth to Perform "See You Again"|publisher=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=March 12, 2016|access-date=January 17, 2024}}</ref>

On January 31, 2020, Khalifa and Puth performed "See You Again" live during halftime of a Portland Trail Blazers-Los Angeles Lakers game at the [[Staples Center]] in Los Angeles, as a tribute to [[Kobe Bryant]], his daughter Gianna and seven other victims of the [[2020 Calabasas helicopter crash|Calabasas helicopter crash]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/8549856/wiz-khalifa-charlie-puth-kobe-bryant-tribute-see-you-again|title=Wiz Khalifa & Charlie Puth Pay Tribute to Kobe Bryant at Lakers Game With 'See You Again': Watch|author=Hilary Hughes|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=February 1, 2020|access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref> On January 15, 2024, Puth and [[The War and Treaty]] performed "See You Again" along with "[[I'll Be There for You (The Rembrandts song)|I'll Be There for You]]" at the [[75th Primetime Emmy Awards]], during the In Memoriam segment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ew.com/emmys-in-memoriam-stars-pay-tribute-to-norman-lear-andre-braugher-and-more-8426515|title=Emmys In Memoriam honors Norman Lear, André Braugher, and more|publisher=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=January 15, 2024|access-date=January 17, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/matthew-perry-tribute-emmys-in-memoriam-friends-theme-song-plays-1235873173/|title=Matthew Perry Honored at Emmys as Emotional Cover of 'Friends' Theme Song Plays During In Memoriam Tribute|publisher=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=January 15, 2024|access-date=January 16, 2024}}</ref>
sections.text:
Khalifa and Puth performed "See You Again" live on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in March 2015 and on an episode of Saturday Night Live in May 2015. Diesel also performed the song live as a tribute to Paul Walker during the 2015 MTV Movie Awards. Khalifa and Puth reprised the song in a performance on The Ellen DeGeneres Show in April 2015. Khalifa and Puth also performed the song at the 2016 Kids' Choice Awards.

On January 31, 2020, Khalifa and Puth performed "See You Again" live during halftime of a Portland Trail Blazers-Los Angeles Lakers game at the Staples Center in Los Angeles, as a tribute to Kobe Bryant, his daughter Gianna and seven other victims of the Calabasas helicopter crash. On January 15, 2024, Puth and The War and Treaty performed "See You Again" along with "I'll Be There for You" at the 75th Primetime Emmy Awards, during the In Memoriam segment.
